Reduced epithelial adhesion is proposed to disturb eyelid development; conditional Cdh1 and Ctnnd1 deletion in animal models produces features reminiscent of BCD syndrome. The tissue-level steps are not established.
Lip and palate closure depends on adhesion and fusion of the oral epithelia, which strongly express E-cadherin; reduced adhesion is proposed to prevent fusion.
The enamel organ is of oral epithelial origin and expresses E-cadherin; reduced adhesion is proposed to impair tooth germ development.

Sparse hair is part of the ectodermal phenotype; a role for disturbed epithelial adhesion in hair follicle development is inferred from the ectodermal-dysplasia character of the syndrome and has not been studied in BCDS.
Somatic inactivation of the remaining CDH1 allele in gastric epithelium is the established route to diffuse gastric cancer in CDH1 carriers; it has not been studied in the BCDS tumour.

nodes.description: E-cadherin is the core adhesive component of epithelial adherens junctions and is linked through p120 catenin (CTNND1) and other catenins to the cytoskeleton; p120 catenin binding prevents E-cadherin endocytosis. BCDS variants impair the cell adhesion function of the cadherin-catenin complex, weakening epithelial cell-cell adhesion. That the BCDS2 gene CTNND1 encodes the E-cadherin partner p120 catenin places both forms of BCD syndrome on the same adhesion complex.
